pages.heading: Functions, continuity, partials and chain rule

blocks.text: A function z=f(x,y) assigns a value to each allowed pair (x,y). Its limit at (a,b) must be independent of the path of approach. Continuity means that this limit equals f(a,b).

The partial derivative \(u_x\) differentiates in x with the other independent variables fixed; \(u_y\) differentiates in y. The second derivatives are \(u_{xx},u_{xy},u_{yx},u_{yy}\). For three variables there are nine ordered second derivatives.

items.title: Equality of mixed partials
question_paragraphs: When can the order of mixed partial differentiation be interchanged?
paragraphs: A standard sufficient condition is that both mixed second partial derivatives exist and are continuous in a neighbourhood of the point. Then \(u_{xy}=u_{yx}\).
Continuity of u alone does not even guarantee first derivatives. For instance u=|x| is continuous but not differentiable in x at zero.
items.final_answer: Use continuity of the mixed second derivatives as the sufficient condition.

math_mismatch.message: The notebook states this for “any continuous function”. Continuity of the function alone is insufficient; the usual sufficient hypothesis concerns its mixed second partial derivatives.

blocks.text: If \(u=f(x,y)\), \(x=x(t),y=y(t)\), then \(du/dt=u_xx\prime(t)+u_yy\prime(t)\). If x and y depend on parameters s,t, then \(u_s=u_xx_s+u_yy_s\), \(u_t=u_xx_t+u_yy_t\).
The total differential is \(du=u_xdx+u_ydy\), or with three variables add \(u_zdz\).

For the notebook’s composite function \(u=u(r,s,t)\), where r,s,t depend on x,y,z, \(u_x=u_rr_x+u_ss_x+u_tt_x\), \(u_y=u_rr_y+u_ss_y+u_tt_y\), \(u_z=u_rr_z+u_ss_z+u_tt_z\). Here a subscript denotes a partial derivative; products such as \(u_rr_x\) mean \((\partial u/\partial r)(\partial r/\partial x)\).
A homogeneous function satisfies \(f(kx,ky)=k^nf(x,y)\). For example \(x^2y+xy^2\) has degree three.
